interactions.prompt: i need to test my object detector on an actual frame from webots instead of a random noise image. i'm using the city.wbt world which has a BMW with a camera on it. can you write a controller that grabs a frame and runs it through my ObjectDetector
interactions.response: Checked the world file itself to find the camera's actual device name rather than guessing, and confirmed it against the C controller that ships with Webots. Wrote a Python controller that connects to the camera, steps the simulation a few times so the render settles, grabs a frame, converts it from Webots' BGRA byte buffer into a PIL image, and runs it through my detector. Explained each part line by line. Also told me I was on the wrong branch and that the camera in that world is only 128x64 by default so I'd want to increase it.

metaReflection.processEvolution: I gave it more context up front this time, which world I was using and what my detector expected, and got something that worked first go instead of having to go back and forth.
metaReflection.criticalMoment: It didn't guess the camera name, it went and read the world file to check. When I ran it at the default 128x64 resolution it detected nothing, which made sense once I bumped it to 640x480 and it started finding things. Also the first run gave me an empty result and I had to work out that was correct because there was nothing in the camera's view, not a bug.
metaReflection.skillDependency: Knowing that Webots hands you a raw BGRA byte buffer and that you have to convert it before PIL can read it. I'd never have worked that out on my own.
metaReflection.synthesis: Testing on real data instead of made up data changes what you find. My detector "worked" on a noise image in the sense that it didn't crash, but I learned nothing from that until I ran it on an actual camera frame.
